record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop constructive versions of supersymmetric and topological field theories, including a constructive understanding of Montonen-Olive duality for N = 4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills in four dimensions and Seiberg-Witten duality for N = 2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills in four dimensions.

evidence.quote: Develop constructive versions of the now-popular supersymmetric field theories, and topological field theories: develop a constructive understanding of Montonen-Olive duality in N = 4 SUSY Yang-Mills4, and of Seiberg-Witten duality for N = 2 SUSY Yang-Mills4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Provide a mathematically rigorous (constructive) construction of supersymmetric and topological quantum field theories on four-dimensional spacetime, and in particular:

(a) Construct, in the sense of constructive quantum field theory (i.e., as a well-defined probability measure on a suitable space of field configurations, or equivalently as a system of Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader correlation functions satisfying the standard axioms), the N=4 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory in four dimensions with gauge group G and coupling constant τ = θ/(2π) + 4πi/g², and rigorously establish the Montonen–Olive S-duality: namely, prove that the theory with gauge group G and coupling τ is equivalent (as a quantum field theory, with matching of correlation functions of dual observables) to the theory with the Langlands dual gauge group ᴸG and coupling −1/(n_𝔤 τ), and that together with τ → τ + 1 this generates an action of SL(2,ℤ) (or an appropriate congruence subgroup) on the space of such theories.

(b) Construct, in the same rigorous sense, the N=2 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory in four dimensions (with gauge group SU(2), and more generally with matter), and rigorously establish Seiberg–Witten duality: produce the low-energy effective abelian gauge theory on the Coulomb branch parametrized by u ∈ ℂ, identify the Seiberg–Witten elliptic curve and special Kähler geometry governing the prepotential, and prove that the duality group action on the moduli space and on the BPS spectrum holds at the level of the constructed theory.

Determine whether such constructive realizations exist and whether the conjectured dualities can be proved within them.
artifact.status_search_result: No rigorous constructive construction of four-dimensional non-abelian N=4 or N=2 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theories is known, and Montonen–Olive and Seiberg–Witten dualities remain conjectural at the level of constructive QFT. They are widely cited as outstanding open problems in mathematical physics and the Clay-style Yang–Mills existence program.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Yang–Mills Theory (Clay Millennium Problem)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a rigorous 4D quantum Yang–Mills theory with a mass gap remains an open Millennium Problem; supersymmetric versions are a fortiori open.
status_evidence.claim: Even non-supersymmetric 4D Yang–Mills lacks a rigorous constructive definition, so the supersymmetric constructive problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists constructive understanding of Montonen–Olive and Seiberg–Witten dualities among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open in recent surveys of constructive field theory.
